findings.title: Client-controlled query param enables negative-offset pagination path
findings.body: `optimized_pagination=true` plus `enable_advanced_features=True` lets a request opt into `OptimizedCursorPaginator`'s branch that passes an unvalidated, possibly negative `cursor.offset` directly into a queryset slice. Cursor offsets come from the user-supplied `cursor` query param (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative integers and no validation was added). This is an unaudited, user-reachable code path that bypasses the offset sanity checks every other paginator enforces (`BadPaginationError('Pagination offset cannot be negative')`), and the whole feature is unrelated to the stated purpose of this PR (spans buffer). It should be removed or gated behind a real permission check plus validation.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` may be None -> AttributeError 500
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally. For a superuser or staff user who is not a member of the organization, `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None`, so this raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500 for every GET of the audit log endpoint, not just when `optimized_pagination` is passed (Python evaluates the right operand of `or` whenever `is_superuser` is False, and `is_superuser` is False for non-superuser members too — in that case `member` is set, but non-member staff/non-member superuser-less tokens will crash). Reorder/short-circuit with `organization_context.member and ...` and only compute it when needed.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime keys used by the audit log endpoint
findings.body: `get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`, which works only for numeric keys. The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by='-datetime'`, where the attribute is a `datetime`; `math.floor()` on a datetime raises `TypeError`. Any request hitting the optimized branch will 500. The paginator either needs DateTimePaginator-style key conversion or must not be used for datetime ordering.

findings.title: Negative queryset slice raises, contrary to the comment
findings.body: The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', but Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indices/slices (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`). So with `enable_advanced_features` and a negative cursor offset the request fails with an unhandled exception (500) instead of a 400. Additionally `stop` can become negative, producing a nonsensical slice.

findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets for next-page, still passes them through for prev
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes long-standing behavior: a negative offset is now silently clamped on forward pages (masking bad cursors rather than failing), while negative offsets are still forwarded unchanged when `cursor.is_prev`, where they will hit Django's negative-slice error. Also the later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check still uses the raw `offset`, so it no longer matches the actual slice when clamping occurred, which can drop or keep the wrong extra row on prev pages.

findings.title: Span eviction limit hardcoded to 1000 and not aligned with max_segment_spans
findings.body: The new `zpopmin` eviction uses the literal 1000, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` defaults to 1001 and is now unused (the span-count guard was removed from `_load_segment_data`). The cap is no longer configurable and silently drops spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` with no metric/log, so oversized segments lose data invisibly. Pass the limit in as an ARGV from `max_segment_spans` and emit a metric when spans are evicted.

findings.title: Redirect-chain depth limit lowered from 10000 to 1000 without justification
findings.body: The loop bound was reduced from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment about segment trees deeper than the limit not being joined correctly was deleted. Traces with redirect chains between 1000 and 10000 that previously merged correctly will now be split into separate segments. If the reduction is intentional (to bound script runtime), keep a comment stating the consequence; otherwise restore the previous bound.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now dead configuration
findings.body: `_load_segment_data` no longer checks `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`, and the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric is gone, yet `max_segment_spans` remains a constructor parameter. Operators setting it get no effect; the enforcement now lives as a hardcoded 1000 in Lua. Either wire the attribute through to the script or remove the parameter.

findings.title: Module docstring still describes Redis sets, not sorted sets
findings.body: The storage was changed from SET (`sadd`/`sscan`/`sunionstore`) to ZSET (`zadd`/`zscan`/`zunionstore`) with score = `end_timestamp_precise`, but the docstring still says 'Add the ingested span's payload to the set under set_key' and 'span-buf:s:* -- the actual set keys'. It also doesn't mention the new per-segment span eviction, which is the key behavioral change of this PR.

findings.title: No test covers the new span eviction path
findings.body: The core change of this PR is evicting spans once a segment exceeds the size cap (`zpopmin` in add-buffer.lua), plus the switch to score-ordered storage. No test inserts more than the cap to assert that the oldest-by-`end_timestamp_precise` spans are dropped and the newest retained, nor that `redirect_depth`/`span_count` accounting stays correct when both the span_key and parent_key union branches run. Add a test that exceeds the limit.
